subject: Business Models
title: Supply vs Demand Side
description: A quick win: understand Supply vs Demand Side.

hook.text: Airbnb spent years recruiting hosts before marketing to travelers. Supply comes first in most marketplaces.

buildup.text: Without enough supply, buyers leave disappointed. Without enough buyers, sellers leave frustrated.

discovery.text: Most marketplaces subsidize the harder-to-get side. Uber gave drivers guaranteed earnings to build supply.

twist.text: In some markets, demand is scarce. Luxury auction houses compete for rare sellers, not buyers.

climax.text: Understanding which side is constrained determines the entire go-to-market strategy.

punchline.text: Build supply first, demand follows. Most marketplaces start backwards.

quiz.question: Which side do most marketplaces build first?

details.summary: Every marketplace must decide which side to attract first and which to subsidize. The harder side to recruit, usually the supply side, typically needs to be built before demand follows..
details.whyItMatters: Getting the sequencing wrong kills marketplaces. Spending on demand acquisition before supply is ready leads to disappointed users who never return..
takeaways: Supply-side acquisition usually comes first because supply attracts demand naturally
The harder side to recruit should receive subsidies and incentives to participate
Demand without sufficient supply creates bad experiences that kill repeat usage

faq.question: Why is supply usually recruited before demand in marketplaces?
faq.answer: Demand-side users who search a marketplace and find no supply leave disappointed and rarely return. But supply-side participants who list products tolerate waiting for demand as long as the platform is free or low-cost..

faq.question: When should a marketplace focus on demand first?
faq.answer: When supply is abundant and undifferentiated, like restaurant delivery where many restaurants exist. When supply only participates for economic reasons and needs proven demand to justify listing. When the marketplace can guarantee immediate demand through marketing or partnerships.
